title: Kestrel Dispensing Standard: Days Supply of a Prescriptions Travel Refill
content:
The vacation override days supply is the days supply of a Kestrel Prescriptions refill with the fill reason vacation override, dispensed before the refill-eligible date for a patient who is travelling.

## Standard

1. **Prescribed daily units.** The prescribed daily units are the prescription's written quantity divided by its written days supply.
2. **Days on hand.** The days of medication still on hand from the most recent refill are that refill's days supply dispensed less the calendar days from its dispensing date, as day 0, to today, never below zero.
3. **Owed days.** Any owed units still standing on the prescription — the units booked on its owed-balance entries less the units completed and the units cancelled — divided by the prescribed daily units, are the owed days.
4. **Days supply.** The vacation override days supply is the class's largest vacation override days supply less the days on hand and less the owed days; the result is never below zero and is taken down to whole days.

## Worked example (hypothetical Non-Controlled Maintenance Prescription, class figure 90 days)

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| Written quantity and days supply | 60 units for 30 days, so 2 daily units |
| Most recent refill | 30 days supply, dispensed on day 0 |
| Today | day 10 |
| Days on hand | 30 less 10: 20 |
| Owed units standing | 5, so 5 divided by 2: 2.5 owed days |
| Days supply | 90 less 20 less 2.5: 67.5, taken down to 67 |

## Other cases (hypothetical)

- The same case with no owed units standing: 90 less 20, which is 70 days.
- A most recent refill of 30 days dispensed 40 days ago: days on hand are never below zero, so 0, and with no owed units the days supply is 90.
- A days supply worked out below zero is 0.
